clue.text: E.g. pool's sides lined with large pointless tiles

indicators.note: the sides are lined with the letter, so it sits inside them

parts.note: a pool's sides are its banks, given here as one example of banks
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone describes tiling round a swimming pool with big plain tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool here is a pond or river, whose sides are banks. In Scrabble the two blank tiles score nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scrabble the blank tiles carry no score value, so they are literally pointless.

clue.text: 50 actors in Narnia butchered Henry V, say

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral 50

indicators.note: the actors sit inside the rearranged place name
butchered means hacked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: A cast of fifty mangles Shakespeare's Henry V in a Narnia setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry V belonged to the House of Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V was a king of the Lancaster royal house, so is an example of this.

clue.text: When cycling, slow mover manages perfectly

indicators.note: cycling means a letter goes round from one end to the other

parts.note: a snail is the proverbial slow mover

explanation.surface: A sluggish cyclist does surprisingly well.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is informal for doing it flawlessly.

clue.text: Bone in back? That's doubtful

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
um is a hesitant noise expressing doubt

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a bone is in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The sceptic is right: the breastbone is at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the flat breastbone in the chest.

clue.text: Import English article into China

indicators.note: the English article is put into the porcelain word

parts.note: Ming is a dynasty whose name stands for fine Chinese porcelain
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A trade instruction to ship an English item into China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is capitalised to hide the porcelain sense; Ming ware is prized china.
explanation.definitionFit: The import of a statement is its significance or sense.

clue.text: Miss tea to overhaul paper cutter

indicators.note: to overhaul something is to take it apart and rebuild it, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: Skip tea break to service the guillotine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper cutter' looks like an office guillotine; it is the artist famous for his cut-paper works.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse made his late cut-outs by snipping painted paper with scissors.

clue.text: Slander, according to boy, gets one imprisoned

parts.note: as per means according to

indicators.note: the numeral is shut up inside the word for boy

parts.note: a son is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lad's allegation gets someone jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging remark attacking someone's reputation.

clue.text: Successful party succeeds without women

definitions.note: singular phrase for a plural answer: the ins are the party in office

indicators.note: without means the letter is left out

parts.note: wins means succeeds

explanation.surface: A winning political group triumphs with no female members.
explanation.definitionFit: The ins are those currently in power, as against the outs in opposition.

clue.text: Windy around top of lighthouse, perfectly calm at sea

indicators.note: the windy word goes around the letter

parts.note: gassy means windy, flatulent

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A storm around a lighthouse contrasts with a flat calm sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A glassy sea is smooth as a mirror, with no ripples.

clue.text: Pepper, say, is ground not minced

indicators.note: ground as in milled, so the letters are crushed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook notes that pepper is milled rather than chopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' and 'minced' both look like kitchen talk; only 'ground' is the signal, and 'not minced' supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepper is an example of a seasoning added to food at table.

clue.text: Creationists gutted admitting very large flash produces this?

definitions.text: Creationists gutted admitting very large flash produces this?

indicators.note: admitting means letting the other pieces inside
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a mo is a moment, a flash

explanation.surface: Dismayed creationists concede that a giant flash, the Big Bang, made the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is the universe, which a vast flash created on the Big Bang theory.

clue.text: Wheat shaped history with the start of agriculture

parts.note: history is what is past

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Farming's beginning is said to have shaped human history.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum flour dough pressed into shapes such as spirals and tubes is the Italian staple.

clue.text: Standard bother about beach outing; naked best?

indicators.note: about signals turning the word round

parts.note: 'Rats!' is an exclamation of annoyance, like 'Bother!'
sands are a beach
a trip is an outing

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: the word best, losing its ends

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a seaside day out and whether nudity is wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' fits the beach scene but strips BEST to ES.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the nickname of the United States flag.

clue.text: Old first lady and VP speaking nicely, raised in privilege

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Eva Perón, Evita, was Argentina's First Lady
Al Gore was US Vice President
RP, Received Pronunciation, is the accent of 'proper' British English

explanation.surface: Political spouses and VPs with posh accents are lifted into privilege.
explanation.definitionFit: A prerogative is an exclusive right or special entitlement.

clue.text: Plump single mother better than the rest

parts.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
I is the Roman numeral one
mum is mother

explanation.surface: A chubby lone parent is praised as superior to everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum describes the most favourable or best possible condition.

clue.text: Backbone dividing Madonna's moving parts

indicators.note: the backbone splits the name in two

parts.note: the Madonna is Mary, mother of Jesus
a chine is an animal's backbone

explanation.surface: The pop star Madonna's spine and her dance moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinery is the working mechanism of a device, its moving components.

clue.text: Some flexible tiles flipping crack

indicators.note: flipping means the run is turned so it reads the other way
some of the words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Bendy tiles keep turning over and cracking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the tiles breaking, but it is the adjective for first-rate troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack troops are the best-trained, select fighting units.

clue.text: Communion with spirits bringing Irishman to church

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irish man takes Holy Communion at church, with spirits nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a gathering at which people try to contact the dead.

clue.text: Anvil's 7 copper parts

indicators.note: copper parts the other word, splitting it in two

parts.note: the answer to 7 down
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's anvil apparently parts seven copper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The incus is one of the small bones of the middle ear, commonly called the anvil.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomists call this middle-ear ossicle the anvil because of its shape.

clue.text: Expert witness's conclusion rubbed out

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: rubbed out is slang for killed

explanation.surface: An expert witness's closing evidence is struck from the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbed out' looks like erased; it is gangster slang for murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled means expert, having trained ability.

clue.text: Leg not broken, but abandoning with puncture

parts.note: pins are slang for legs

indicators.note: the whole word abandons the letter for with

parts.note: something not broken is whole

explanation.surface: An injured leg turns out not to be broken, though it has a puncture wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinhole is a tiny hole such as a pin would make, a small puncture.

clue.text: River vessel, ordinary and waterproof

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
a mac (mackintosh) is a waterproof coat

explanation.surface: A plain river boat with waterproofing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is the American waterway flowing past Washington DC.

clue.text: Religious retreat has converted member of the flock

indicators.note: converted means changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, part of a flock

explanation.surface: A sheep from the congregation has been converted at a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flock' and 'converted' suggest a congregation; the member is a literal sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or spiritual community.

clue.text: Ann is inheriting forged Reynolds picture

indicators.note: forged as in faked, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Ann's inheritance includes a fake painting by Sir Joshua Reynolds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reynolds is not the painter but Debbie Reynolds, and the picture is a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Debbie Reynolds starred in this 1952 movie musical, a picture in the cinema sense.

clue.text: Clean up Toby's first belch

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: pure means clean

indicators.note: first means the opening letter

explanation.surface: Toby is told to tidy up after his first burp.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst out, as a volcano or a belch does.

clue.text: Sweep called back to apologise

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep phones back to say sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweep of a view or of knowledge is its range or extent.

clue.text: Sister nobody listened to

indicators.note: listened to means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: none means nobody

explanation.surface: A sister whom no one paid attention to.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a religious sister in a convent.

clue.text: Car from Finland reversing into field

indicators.note: the reversed name goes into the other word

parts.note: a line of work is a field

indicators.note: reversing means the name is written backwards

parts.note: Suomi is the Finnish name for Finland

explanation.surface: A car from Finland backs into a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious chauffeur-driven vehicle.

clue.text: Wealthy looker gets date on first day

indicators.note: on means placed after, as in an across entry

parts.note: Monday, abbreviated Mon, is the first day of the working week
an eye is what looks

explanation.surface: A good-looking person lands a date on Monday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looker' suggests an attractive person; here it is the organ that looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means having plenty of cash, rich.

clue.text: Shop with c as the first letter becomes chop

indicators.note: the given letter takes the place of the opening letter

parts.note: an outlet is a shop

explanation.surface: A spelling game: change the first letter of shop to c and get chop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's own letter change (s to c, shop to chop) mirrors the wordplay on a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlet is a chop, a small cut of meat taken with the rib.
